body.statement: Restrict the inference result to the binary-treatment submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P^r\) satisfying \(P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1\), the primitive moment map satisfies \((p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathfrak D_+^r\), \(\mathfrak I_a^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) for \(a\in\{d,e\}\), and \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\). Under the fixed known binary-treatment grid and ranges, \(\Pr_P\{(p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathcal H_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), and therefore \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P^r:\,P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1}\Pr_P\{\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\). Replacing the ATE image by either \(\mathfrak I_a^r\) image gives simultaneous coverage of both target-arm closures on the same event. Coverage holds at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) because projection precedes application of the exact-set map; zero-mass candidate cells are excluded without excluding the strictly positive population pair fixed by \(\mathcal J=\operatorname{Supp}_P(D,Z)\).
body.justification: Projection of the explicit primitive-moment image preserves finite-sample honesty despite branch discontinuity.
body.gap: BanKedagni2022 treats intersection-bound outer formulas, while calibrated projection and perturbed-LP methods do not directly cover a support-filtered union whose components disappear.
body.consumer: NLSYM-style and air-pollution analyses can report a conservative confidence region for the entire exact population set, including a zero-slack diagnostic.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a law in the stated binary-treatment model.  For each positive-mass cell define
\[
 p_j(P)=P(C=c_j),\qquad
 \omega_j(P)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbf{1}\{C=c_j\}\frac{Y-\ell_{d_j}}{u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j}}\right].
\]
Assumptions \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\), \(\text{ass:known-grid}\), and \(\text{ass:known-ranges}\) give \(p_j(P)>0\), \(\sum_jp_j(P)=1\), and \(0\le\omega_j(P)\le p_j(P)\).  In LEI mode, \(\text{ass:target-overlap}\) gives \(\sigma_D(P)>0\) because \(d\ne e\) both have positive probability, and \(\text{ass:lei-scale}\) gives \(\sigma_Z(P)>0\).  These are exactly the two positive variances required by \(\mathfrak D_+^r\).  Hence
\[
 (p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathfrak D_+^r.                                          \tag{35}
\]
Division is made only after (35): conditional expectation gives
\[
 \ell_{d_j}+(u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j})\frac{\omega_j(P)}{p_j(P)}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y\mid C=c_j]=m_j.                                                \tag{36}
\]
Substitution of (36) into \(\text{def:primitive-sharp-map}\) reproduces, term by term, the observed means, centered treatment and instrument scores, branch polytopes, slack programs, eligible branches, and endpoints defined from \(P\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak I_a^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_a^r(P),\qquad
 \mathfrak I_\Delta^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P).                 \tag{37}
\]
This is an equality of observed-law sharp-closure functionals; their equality to the closures of the causal identified sets follows from \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\) and \(\text{prop:ate-product-coupling}\).

We next prove the finite-sample probability bound.  For a random variable \(X\in[0,1]\) with mean \(\mu\), convexity gives \(e^{tX}\le1-X+Xe^t\), hence
\[
 \mathbb E e^{t(X-\mu)}\le e^{-t\mu}(1-\mu+\mu e^t)\le e^{t^2/8}.             \tag{38}
\]
For the last inequality, the logarithm on the middle term is zero with zero derivative at \(t=0\), and its second derivative is the variance of a Bernoulli variable under exponential tilting, hence is at most \(1/4\); integrating twice proves (38).  Exponential Markov inequality, independence from \(\text{ass:iid}\), and minimization at \(t=4\eta\) now give
\[
 P\!\left(\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i-\mathbb EX_i\right|>\eta\right)
 \le2e^{-2n\eta^2}.                                                            \tag{39}
\]
This is the bounded-variable argument of \cite{Hoeffding1963}, reproduced here in the exact form used.

Each of the \(2K\) variables defining \(\widehat p_j\) and \(\widehat\omega_j\) lies in \([0,1]\).  Applying (39) and the union bound at \(\eta=\eta_n\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{(p(P),\omega(P))\notin\mathcal H_n\}
 &\le4K\exp(-2n\eta_n^2)\\
 &=4K\exp\{-\log(4K/\alpha)\}=\alpha.                                       \tag{40}
 \end{aligned}
\]
On the event complementary to (40), (35) shows that the true primitive pair is one of the candidates in \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathfrak D_+^r\).  Equations (37) and \(\text{def:projection-region}\) then imply pathwise
\[
 \mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n.                                 \tag{41}
\]
The same single event implies the analogous inclusion for both arm images, so their coverages are simultaneous.  Since (40) holds for every law in the displayed model and every \(n\), taking the infimum over \(P\) proves the uniform claim.

No continuity or branch-selection assertion entered (40)--(41).  In particular, if a population branch has \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\), the true primitive pair is still projected before the exact-set map is applied.  Empirical candidate pairs with zero masses are excluded from \(\mathfrak D_+^r\), but (35) shows that the population pair is never excluded.  Thus the conclusion remains valid at the support-eligibility boundary.
